newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - March 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - March 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Energy Minister Noor Uddin Khan on Sunday said the country would have an additional 390 megawatt of electricity by September.
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has decided to reject the applications by companies willing to float shares if those or their directors are found as bank loan defaulters.
Former President Hussain Muahammad Ershad was shifted to a hospital on Sunday with cardio-vascular problem.
Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer will arrive in Dhaka on April 7 on a two-day visit to Bangladesh.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Sunday instructed police to go allout fo ensuring the security of public life.
Some 271 tribal families returned home from refugee camps in India's Tripura state during the last three days, completing the first phase of the repatriation process.
The World Bank has said the existing corporate tax system, controls on foreign exchange and weak legal framework increase the cost of doing business in Bangladesh.
China on Sunday approved an interest free loan of 30 million Yuan for Bangladesh. REUTER
